answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before its Wesolowski proof is accepted. A GPU can run many chains for separate clones, but cannot shortcut the dependency within any one chain, so each clone incurs real elapsed time and compute. This raises the cost of rapid Sybil creation; it does not make identities unique. A juniper, a gale, or an orchard cannot alter that timing constraint.
